mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Federal Funds Rate (FEDFUNDS) by more than 0.5% in a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in Real Final Sales (RSAFS) over three consecutive months indicates weakening consumer demand, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings expectations are revised downwards.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between RSAFS declines and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in a month signals labor market weakness, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate slower economic growth and reduced corporate earnings.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between UNRATE increases and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in Industrial Production (INDPRO) over three consecutive months signals strengthening supply-side fundamentals, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings expectations improve.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between INDPRO increases and positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in Housing Starts (HOUST) by more than 5% in a month signals strengthening demand in the housing market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as related sectors benefit from increased activity.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between HOUST increases and positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) over three consecutive months signals easing inflationary pressures, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as the likelihood of monetary policy easing increases.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between CPIAUCSL declines and positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When Nonfarm Payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 and the Unemployment Rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.2% in the same month, it signals a tightening labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investor sentiment improves.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the joint effect of PAYEMS and UNRATE changes on SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When Real GDP (GDPC1) grows by more than 2% year-over-year and Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) remains stable (change within +/- 0.5%), it signals strong real economic growth without inflationary pressures, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings expectations improve.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY growth > 2% & CPIAUCSL change within +/- 0.5%
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the joint effect of GDPC1 growth and stable CPIAUCSL on SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
